data.narrative:
PlanQC is a Series A quantum computing company that has raised $50M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a sector universe of 11 total comparables—3 public (IonQ, Rigetti, D-Wave) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum and Infleqtion—though the quantum computing sector remains sufficiently nascent that narrow stage-and-tier matched peer sets are sparse.

Given data constraints, the analysis relies on stage-progression methodology. Using the $50M total raised as a proxy baseline and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to later-stage advancement, this method implies a valuation of $100M. A peer-median approach was not applicable; while six quantum computing peers exist in the broader dataset, fewer than three comparables meet the confluence of same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar-tier filtering criteria required for reliable benchmarking. Applying an all-sector median would introduce excessive distortion.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $85M to $115M, centered at $100M. Key uncertainties include the early stage of quantum hardware commercialization, which limits the availability of valuation precedent, and PlanQC's specific technical pathway relative to the divergent architectural approaches represented across its peer set. Investors should weight this analysis as preliminary; a second method would strengthen conviction once additional comparable transactions emerge or company-specific financial metrics (revenue, burn rate, customer traction) become available for analysis.
